statement: Let n = len(arr1). Call a sequence b of length n obtainable if for every i with 0 <= i < n, either b[i] = arr1[i] or there exists j with 0 <= j < len(arr2) and b[i] = arr2[j]. Call b increasing if b[i] < b[i+1] for every 0 <= i < n-1. Let cost(b) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and b[i] != arr1[i]. The function returns a result r such that either: (a) r = -1 and there is no obtainable increasing sequence b, or (b) r >= 0, there exists an obtainable increasing sequence b with cost(b) = r, and every obtainable increasing sequence b satisfies cost(b) >= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr1) <= 2000, 1 <= len(arr2) <= 2000, 0 <= arr1[i] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= i < len(arr1), and 0 <= arr2[j] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= j < len(arr2).

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, or overflow) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr1) <= 2000, 1 <= len(arr2) <= 2000, 0 <= arr1[i] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= i < len(arr1), and 0 <= arr2[j] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= j < len(arr2).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, either r = -1 or 0 <= r <= len(arr1).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr1) <= 2000, 1 <= len(arr2) <= 2000, 0 <= arr1[i] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= i < len(arr1), and 0 <= arr2[j] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= j < len(arr2).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if arr1 is strictly increasing, meaning arr1[i] < arr1[i+1] for every 0 <= i < len(arr1)-1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr1) <= 2000, 1 <= len(arr2) <= 2000, 0 <= arr1[i] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= i < len(arr1), and 0 <= arr2[j] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= j < len(arr2).

statement: Let n = len(arr1). The function returns r = -1 if and only if there is no sequence b of length n such that: (i) for every i with 0 <= i < n, either b[i] = arr1[i] or there exists j with 0 <= j < len(arr2) and b[i] = arr2[j], and (ii) b[i] < b[i+1] for every 0 <= i < n-1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr1) <= 2000, 1 <= len(arr2) <= 2000, 0 <= arr1[i] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= i < len(arr1), and 0 <= arr2[j] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= j < len(arr2).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, there exists a sequence b of length len(arr1) such that: (i) for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr1), either b[i] = arr1[i] or there exists j with 0 <= j < len(arr2) and b[i] = arr2[j]; (ii) b[i] < b[i+1] for every 0 <= i < len(arr1)-1; and (iii) the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(arr1) and b[i] != arr1[i] is exactly r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr1) <= 2000, 1 <= len(arr2) <= 2000, 0 <= arr1[i] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= i < len(arr1), and 0 <= arr2[j] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= j < len(arr2).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, for every sequence b of length len(arr1) satisfying: (i) for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr1), either b[i] = arr1[i] or there exists j with 0 <= j < len(arr2) and b[i] = arr2[j]; and (ii) b[i] < b[i+1] for every 0 <= i < len(arr1)-1, the number of indices i with b[i] != arr1[i] is at least r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr1) <= 2000, 1 <= len(arr2) <= 2000, 0 <= arr1[i] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= i < len(arr1), and 0 <= arr2[j] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= j < len(arr2).

statement: If the function returns r on (arr1, arr2) and returns r' on (arr1, arr2'), then r = r'.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr1) <= 2000, 1 <= len(arr2) <= 2000, 0 <= arr1[i] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= i < len(arr1), 0 <= arr2[j] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= j < len(arr2), and arr2' is any slice of i64 with 1 <= len(arr2') <= 2000 such that for every integer v, v occurs in arr2' if and only if v occurs in arr2.

statement: Let r be the result of the function on (arr1, arr2) and r' the result on (arr1, arr2'). If r >= 0, then r' >= 0 and r' <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr1) <= 2000, 1 <= len(arr2) <= 2000, 0 <= arr1[i] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= i < len(arr1), 0 <= arr2[j] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= j < len(arr2), and arr2' is any slice of i64 with 1 <= len(arr2') <= 2000 and 0 <= arr2'[j] <= 10^9 for every j, such that every value occurring in arr2 also occurs in arr2'.

statement: If the function returns r on (arr1, arr2) and returns r' on (arr1', arr2'), then r = r'.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr1) <= 2000, 1 <= len(arr2) <= 2000, 0 <= arr1[i] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= i < len(arr1), 0 <= arr2[j] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= j < len(arr2), and F is a function from integers to integers such that F(x) is in [0, 10^9] for every value x occurring in arr1 or arr2, and F(x) < F(y) whenever x < y and both x and y occur in arr1 or arr2. Define arr1'[i] = F(arr1[i]) and arr2'[j] = F(arr2[j]).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, the integer len(arr1) - r equals the maximum, over all sequences b of length len(arr1) such that: (i) for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr1), either b[i] = arr1[i] or there exists j with 0 <= j < len(arr2) and b[i] = arr2[j]; and (ii) b[i] < b[i+1] for every 0 <= i < len(arr1)-1, of the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(arr1) and b[i] = arr1[i].
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr1) <= 2000, 1 <= len(arr2) <= 2000, 0 <= arr1[i] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= i < len(arr1), and 0 <= arr2[j] <= 10^9 for every 0 <= j < len(arr2).
